result.result:
The app is built and working. `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` runs it, and logging in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. The production build passes with no warnings. I ran a browser script through the whole app and every check passed with no console errors. Three checks failed on the first runs; each was my test checking before the screen had updated, and repeating them with a short wait confirmed the app behaves correctly.

**What the browser checks covered**
- **Routing and login:** the guards and redirects work. Submitting an empty login form puts both fields into an error state. A successful login writes `isLoggedIn: true` and goes to the dashboard. Sign Out clears it.
- **Dashboard:** there are 4 metric tiles and 7 chart bars, and a new log line appears every 3 seconds.
- **User menu:** it opens leftward and stays fully on screen at 1280px and 420px widths. It closes on an outside click or Escape.
- **Team Members, all four operations:**
  - **Edit:** splits the name, saves with `PUT`, and the table updates.
  - **Invite:** shows required-field errors, adds the member with `POST`, and the form resets.
  - **Delete:** removes the row with `DELETE`, and closes on a backdrop click.
  - **Details:** shows "Member since January 2024", and its fields are read-only.
  - **Edit → Delete user:** keeps the selected member.

**Where the spec and Figma disagreed:** the spec's wording decided the text and the Figma frames decided the layout.
- **Data Summary:** Figma has 7 dashboard cards, while the spec lists 8 tiles. The Figma card named "Data Summary" holds the throughput chart plus a stats row. I followed that, so Request Throughput and Data Summary share one card (with a small "Data Summary" label) instead of adding a card that isn't in the design.
- **Taken from Figma:** the "System Overview" heading and "Last updated" line on the dashboard, the divider above "Don't have an account?" on the login card, and dates shown as `Jan 2024` in the table.
- **Taken from the spec:** separate Avatar and Name columns, Details as the least-emphasised action, uppercase tile titles, monospace logs, and nav items "Dashboard" and "Team Members" (Figma shows Overview, Metrics, Logs, Settings).
- **Badge colours from Figma:** Admin red, Editor blue, Viewer grey; Active green, Inactive grey. The Error Rate trend is amber, as in Figma, rather than red.
- **Not included:** the "Online" badge in the Figma dashboard header, because it doesn't appear on the Users frame.

**Problems in the component library**
- **List dividers don't render.** The `divided` option on the list never draws its lines. I add the dividers from the app's own styles without touching the library's internals.
- **No header slot.** The header has no place to put the user menu, so I position the menu over its right edge.
- **Header and footer links reload the page,** which would reset the mock data. I catch those clicks and route them inside the app instead.
- **Broken avatar images stay broken.** The avatar component doesn't fall back to initials when an image fails to load. I detect failed images on the users page and show initials instead.
- **Modal dividers left out.** Figma draws lines between the modal header, body and footer. The library's modal has none, and I didn't add them.

**Values the design tokens don't cover:** I used no raw colours, and every spacing, size and colour comes from a design token, except:
- **Large text:** Figma's 26px metric values and 20px dashboard title have no token. I used the 22px and 18px tokens instead.
- **Fonts:** there's no font-family token, so the Inter and monospace stacks are written directly.
- **Shapes:** Figma's 12px modal and login-card corners have no token (I used the 10px one), and there's no token for its card shadows, so I left them out.
- **Breakpoints:** CSS can't use variables in media queries, so the two breakpoints are plain pixel values.
- **Chart and log heights:** these are worked out from spacing tokens, because no height token fits.

**Setup notes**
- The folder had a lockfile that had pulled in Angular 21. I removed it and pinned Angular to 19.2.
- I raised the per-component style size limit in `angular.json` so the dashboard stylesheet doesn't trigger a build warning.

All the Figma data loaded, so nothing visual was built without checking the frames.
